{"self_assessment": "Impact: I took ownership of the upper tail fork (stroke 3) early and kept it moving. I laid it from the start, carried it on from the crossing near the tail, and re-laid it so it joined the line cleanly. I also used my free time to inspect the table and report what I saw. One finding was that the chain stalled at the end of the start row, where one domino sat too tight against the next, and I told the table so they could act on it.

Execution: I picked one piece of work and stayed on it quietly. I built the upper fork in several passes and stood dominoes back up when needed. I ran several close inspections to check how far the chain would carry and where pieces were unconnected. I kept my findings short and specific so the others could use them.

Collaboration: I confirmed my role out loud as soon as it was assigned, so there was no overlap with the lower fork. I stayed off the nose once Jack, Sofia and Hana were working there, so we didn't undo each other's dominoes. I shared my diagnosis with the table instead of working around it alone.

Leadership: I didn't set the plan, since Jack and Hana led the design. I led by reliability: I took a clearly bounded piece, finished it, and used my spare time to inspect and give the team accurate information. In the last minutes I deliberately held back so I wouldn't add risk to a crowded area.", "my_share_percent": 20}
